comment: The object-oriented surface over the natives (docs/language.md, "Members"; docs/research/oo-surface.md). tools/gen-members.cs writes src/Ffx.Atel.Game/Members.g.cs from this file and data/natives.json; the compiler lowers each member onto its native, and the decompiler writes the member where the bytes allow. "groups": the containers members go into: "component" (a property of every worker, Turn.Start()), "indexed" (a property of every worker indexed by the native's first argument, Sprites[3].Show(…)), "static" (an engine-wide static class, Wait.Frames(…)); a group with "properties" ({"enum", "get", "set"}) has a property per member of the enum, read by the "get" native and written by the "set" one with the member as the argument after the receiver (Actors[Target.AllPly].Hp = 0 is Btl.SetActorsProperty(Target.AllPly, ActorProperty.Hp, 0); Self.Hp is Btl.GetSelfProperty(ActorProperty.Hp)); a group whose name has a dot is a static group nested in the one before the dot ("Camera.Eye": Camera.Eye.AimAt(…)). "members": native id -> "member" (a path: "Pos" a member of the worker, "Turn.Start" a member of a group, "Camera.Eye.AimAt" a member of a nested group, "Pos.X" a component of a Vector3 property), "as" ("method", the default; "get" or "set" for a property), "worker" (the native's first argument is the worker it acts on: unqualified the member passes Common.GetWorkerId(-1), Tidus.Member passes Tidus's number, Workers[n].Member passes n), "vector" (the setter's three float arguments are a Vector3), "bool" (the setter's value is 0 or 1: a bool property); "choice" (a member several natives share, one per value of its first argument, a constant of the enum "choiceType" names: Camera.Eye.Shake(ShakeKind.SineFadeOut, …) is 0x605d; the compiler picks the native by it and does not pass it), and "params", the member's parameters after it, where the natives' own differ in name or kind. Names come from the native's verified name and its summary; a member names nothing the native's documentation does not say.

Turn.summary: Turns the worker over several frames: set the angle (<see cref="TurnControl.Yaw"/>) and the time (<see cref="TurnControl.SetFrames"/>), then <see cref="TurnControl.Start"/> the turn and <see cref="TurnControl.Wait"/> for it.

Move.summary: Moves the worker to a point over several frames: set the point (<see cref="MoveControl.Target"/>) and the speed (<see cref="MoveControl.Speed"/>), then <see cref="MoveControl.Start"/> the move and <see cref="MoveControl.Wait"/> for it.

Motion.summary: The animation the worker's model plays. Assign a motion to set it (<c>Motion = 0x71050;</c>); the members play a motion, wait for it to end and give the model its own stand, walk and run motions back.

Neck.summary: The head of the worker's model: what it looks at and how fast it turns there.

Actors.summary: The battle's actors, picked by a selector: <c>Actors[Target.AllPly].Hp = 0;</c> sets the property of every actor the selector picks, <c>Actors[Target.Own].Hp</c> reads it (averaged over the picked actors).

Self.summary: The worker's own battle actor: <c>Self.Hp</c> reads its HP, <c>Self.Hp = 0;</c> sets it.

Wait.summary: Pauses the entry: for some frames (<see cref="Wait.Frames"/>), some seconds (<see cref="Wait.Seconds"/>) or for ever. Scripts run at 30 frames a second.

Camera.summary: The camera: where it is (<see cref="Camera.Eye"/>), the point it looks at (<see cref="Camera.Focus"/>), the screens it draws to (<see cref="Camera.Screen"/>), and its roll, zoom and blur.

Camera.Eye.summary: The camera's eye, the point the camera sits at: where it is, how it moves there, the limits it keeps to, its path and its shakes.

Camera.Focus.summary: The point the camera looks at: where it is, how it moves there, the limits it keeps to, its path and its shakes.

Camera.Screen.summary: The screens the camera draws to, by number: their shakes and moves.

Voice.summary: The voice line: prepare it (<see cref="Voice.Prepare"/>), play it (<see cref="Voice.Play"/>), wait while it plays (<see cref="Voice.IsPlaying"/>), stop it.

doc.summary: Sets how close the player has to come to talk to the worker; most scripts use 13.
Sets the angle, in radians, within which the player has to face the worker to talk to it; most scripts use 1.047 (60 degrees).
Releases what the worker is attached to (a model, a camera) without freeing its data.
Sets how the worker's model keeps to the ground: 0 holds it at the ground's height, 1 snaps it onto the ground, 2 lets it float and bob, as on water.
Turns the automatic mouth movement of the worker's model on or off.
Sets how fast the worker turns, in radians a frame; the default is π/64.
Sets a second turn speed, in radians a frame (default π/64). What the game uses it for is not known yet.
Returns which kind of turn the worker has left: bit 0 is set while it still has to turn, bit 1 when the turn is a large one.
Returns how many frames the worker's turn takes, given the frames for a small turn and for a large one.
Sets the four motions the worker's model plays when it turns, one per kind of turn.
Sets the speed of the worker's move; most scripts use 16.
Sets how close to its target the worker has to come for its move to end.
Sets the direction of the worker's move, in radians, wrapped into one turn.
Sets how long the worker's next move takes, for the timed moves: the frames done so far and the total.
Returns the vertical angle from the worker to its move target.
The motion the worker's model plays now.
Plays the model's own motion for what it is doing (standing, walking or running).
Sets the speed of the worker's model's motion.
The frame the worker's model's motion is at, in 256ths of a frame.
Turns the neck control of the worker's model on or off: when it is on, the head turns towards the neck's target.
Makes the worker's model look at another worker, by its number.
Makes the worker's model look at a point.
Makes the worker's model look at the camera.
Sets how fast the head of the worker's model turns towards its target.
Hides everything on the screen beyond depth <paramref name="z"/>, with a full-screen mask (plane 0 or 1).
Suspends the camera channel of worker <paramref name="worker"/>; <see cref="Camera.Resume"/> starts it again.
Starts the camera channel of worker <paramref name="worker"/> again after <see cref="Camera.Suspend"/>.
Makes the eye follow the focus list in a variable; <see cref="Camera.Eye.SetFocusList1"/> does the same with flag 1.
Circles the eye around two battle actors, at a distance plus the actors' size.
Places the eye around two battle actors: a height, a yaw and a pitch in degrees, and a distance.
Starts the eye's move to its set position over <paramref name="frames"/> frames, at an even speed.
As <see cref="Camera.Eye.MoveEased"/>, with move mode 1.
Adds the eye's current place to its built-in path (at most 32 points; a path needs 3 or more).

Starts a shake of the eye (the camera's position): the angle of its wave steps by <paramref name="speed"/> each frame, scaled by <paramref name="amplitude"/> (MsCameraShake). The kind picks the native; <see cref="ShakeKind"/> says how each moves.

params.kind: How it moves: the wave and whether it fades out, fades in or stays (each kind is its own native).
params.which: The axes to shake, bits 0-2 (x, y, z).
params.speed: The angle the wave advances each frame.
params.jitter: A random range for the amplitude (each frame scaled by (32 + j) / 32, j within it); 0 for none.

doc.summary: Makes the focus point follow worker <paramref name="target"/>, raised by <paramref name="yOffset"/>.
Circles the focus point around two battle actors, at a distance plus the actors' size.
Places the focus point around two battle actors: a height, a yaw and a pitch in degrees, and a distance. The most common battle shot.
Starts the focus point's move to its set position over <paramref name="frames"/> frames, at an even speed.
As <see cref="Camera.Focus.MoveEased"/>, with move mode 1.
Sets the focus point's move-stat byte (<c>MsCameraMoveStat</c>, the value inverted).
Adds a line limit to the focus point: the segment from (<paramref name="x1"/>, <paramref name="z1"/>) to (<paramref name="x2"/>, <paramref name="z2"/>) with radius <paramref name="r"/>; at most 5.
Removes the focus point's limits (the line, height and path limits added before).
Adds the focus point's current place to its built-in path.

doc.summary: Stops the shakes of a screen.
Waits until screen <paramref name="screen"/> has stopped moving.
Prepares a voice line, so that <see cref="Voice.Play"/> can start it at once; does nothing while one is prepared.
